ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only a describing word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

2. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. happiness
   C. quickly
   D. run

3. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

4. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

5. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

6. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

7. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

9. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

10. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. No full stops
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

12. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

2. D — run

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

11. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

12. A — Where is the library?

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
